markers.title: The drop asks a question instead of leaving a hole
markers.finding: There was no automatic leave when a part-time person dropped a shift, and the manager then received a compliance warning for not meeting their contracted hours. One asked directly for an option to mark a dropped shift as leave with or without pay.
markers.decision: Dropping the shift raises the four things it could become, with the cost of each, at the moment the decision is live.
markers.rejected: Deleting the shift and reporting the shortfall later, which is what produced the warning and the make-up pay.

markers.title: Every option carries its price
markers.finding: Make-up pay and overtime arrived at the pay run with no explanation attached and no record of a decision having been made.
markers.decision: Three of the four options cost nothing extra and one costs a specific amount. The figure comes from the rule that would have raised the warning.
markers.rejected: Ranking the options by policy. A manager short-staffed on a Thursday is weighing coverage against cost, and needs both numbers.

markers.title: A date range writes the shifts
markers.finding: A leave shift had to be created by hand after approval, one day at a time. A week was five entries. Extended leave, up to a year, was described as being put in shift by shift.
markers.decision: The dates produce the list of shifts they cover, read from the published roster, and approving writes all of them. Coverage lost becomes an open shift rather than silence.
markers.rejected: Bulk entry as a separate tool, which is a second thing to learn for the case that matters most.

markers.title: Consent is captured, not assumed
markers.finding: Consent was not captured when leave was entered on somebody's behalf, and a consent workflow went onto the backlog as a ranked ticket.
markers.decision: Entering leave for someone sends them what they are agreeing to, in hours and dollars against their balance, and writes nothing until they answer.
markers.rejected: A tickbox on the manager's side saying consent was obtained, which records the manager's memory rather than the person's agreement.
